seoTitle: Add a Newsletter Form in Elementor for Free
metaDescription: Learn how to add a free newsletter signup form in Elementor using Fluent Forms and connect it to FluentCRM, without needing Elementor Pro.
intro: Collecting email subscribers directly on your Elementor pages doesn't require Elementor Pro if you use Fluent Forms alongside FluentCRM. This guide covers creating the form, embedding it inside Elementor, and connecting submissions to your CRM for follow-up.

steps.heading: Create the newsletter form in Fluent Forms
steps.body: Use Fluent Forms' free builder to design a simple subscription form with the fields you want visitors to fill out.

steps.heading: Embed the form inside Elementor
steps.body: Add Fluent Forms' shortcode or widget into an Elementor page or section, no coding or premium widgets required.

steps.heading: Connect Fluent Forms to FluentCRM
steps.body: Link the form to FluentCRM so every new subscriber is automatically added to your email list for future campaigns.

steps.heading: Style the form to match your page
steps.body: Adjust the form's appearance within Elementor's editor so it fits naturally with the rest of your page design.

steps.heading: Test the form before publishing
steps.body: Submit a test entry to confirm subscribers land correctly in FluentCRM before making the page live.

faq.question: Can I add this form without Elementor Pro?
faq.answer: Yes, Fluent Forms integrates into Elementor's free version using its shortcode or widget, so Elementor Pro isn't required.

faq.question: Is FluentCRM free to use?
faq.answer: FluentCRM offers a free tier suitable for basic email list management and automation, alongside paid plans for advanced features.

faq.question: Why isn't my newsletter form showing up in Elementor?
faq.answer: This is usually caused by the shortcode not being pasted correctly or a caching issue — clearing cache and re-checking the shortcode placement often resolves it.

faq.question: Can I customize the form's design in Elementor?
faq.answer: Yes, once embedded, you can adjust spacing, colors, and layout around the form using Elementor's standard styling tools.
